property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the provided _baseToken argument (i.e. baseToken() == _baseToken) after initialize returns; the mutant unconditionally sets baseToken to address(0) and thus violates this property for inputs where _baseToken != address(0).

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed pool's baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed to initialize (reference); the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so there exist inputs where baseToken != _baseToken and the property fails.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the _baseToken parameter (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize returns); the mutant swaps and sets baseToken == _nft, so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken and the property fails.

For any call to initialize(..., _baseToken, ...), the contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument (reference preserves the provided base token), whereas the mutant overrides baseToken to msg.sender and thus can make baseToken != _baseToken for some inputs.

For all calls to initialize(..., _nft, ...), the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed (reference preserves provided NFT address); the mutant that assigns msg.sender to nft instead will make nft() differ from the provided _nft for some inputs.

For any initialize parameters the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed to initialize; the mutant that doubles the assignment will cause changeFee != _changeFee for some fuzzed _changeFee values.

After initialize(...) completes, the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed in; the mutant that sets changeFee = 0 breaks this for any _changeFee != 0 (the fuzzer will find such inputs).

For all initialize(...) calls, the contract's changeFee equals the _changeFee parameter provided to initialize; the mutant sets changeFee from _feeRate instead, so there exist inputs where changeFee != _changeFee and the property is violated.

For any initialize(...) call that succeeds on the reference contract, the stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate (i.e. feeRate == _feeRate); the mutant clamps >5000 inputs to 0 causing stored feeRate != _feeRate for some inputs (>5000).

For any call to initialize, the reference implementation either reverts when _feeRate > 5000 or, if it returns, stores feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant instead never reverts for >5000 (it stores 0), so there exist fuzzed _feeRate inputs (>5000) where the mutant returns but the reference would have reverted — we assert that a successful initialize implies stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate (so the reference never returns with a different stored feeRate, but the mutant can).
For any call to initialize that returns (does not revert), the stored feeRate equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant can return for inputs >5000 while storing feeRate == 0, violating this equality.

For any call to initialize that completes successfully, the contract's public feeRate equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant clamps >5000 inputs to 0 and thus can return successfully while feeRate != _feeRate.

For every call to initialize(...) that does NOT revert, the stored feeRate equals the value returned by the public getter feeRate(); the mutant can accept inputs >5000 (by not reverting) but store 0, breaking this invariant for some fuzzed _feeRate > 5000.

For any inputs, a successful initialize call always sets feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate (i.e. c.feeRate() == _feeRate); the mutant that assigns initialized = true before setting feeRate allows reentrancy during initialization to observe an unset/zero feeRate and thus can lead to c.feeRate() != _feeRate for some inputs (when an adversarial nft or baseToken performs a reentrant call).

For any inputs, a successful initialize(...) call on the correct contract sets feeRate to the provided _feeRate; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning feeRate) can be re-entered by a malicious NFT contract during initialize, causing initialize to complete with feeRate != _feeRate for some fuzzed inputs.

For any inputs, a successful call to initialize(...) on the correct contract always results in c.feeRate() == _feeRate; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning feeRate) can be re-entered by a malicious NFT contract during initialize causing feeRate to remain 0 (or differ) for some fuzzed inputs, so the property is that feeRate equals the provided _feeRate after initialize returns.

For any inputs, after initialize(...) returns on the correct contract, feeRate() equals the provided _feeRate; the mutant that sets initialized = true before assigning feeRate can be re-entered by a malicious NFT contract during initialization causing feeRate() to differ from the provided _feeRate for some fuzzed inputs.

For any inputs, a successful call to initialize(...) on the correct contract always results in c.feeRate() == _feeRate after the call returns; the mutant (which sets initialized = true before assigning feeRate) can be re-entered by a malicious ERC721 token during initialize causing feeRate() to differ from the provided _feeRate for some fuzzed inputs.

For any inputs to initialize where the provided _feeRate is ≤ 5000, the correct contract stores feeRate equal to the supplied _feeRate; the mutant incorrectly overwrites feeRate to the constant 100 for some inputs (e.g. when _feeRate != 100) causing a mismatch.

After any successful call to initialize(...) the contract's public `initialized()` getter becomes true; the mutant that omits setting `initialized = true` will leave it false for some inputs (i.e. after a successful initialize call).

For any call to initialize(...) when the contract was not initialized, the reference implementation always sets initialized == true after successful initialization; the mutant leaves initialized false for some nonzero _feeRate, breaking that property.

For any admissible initialize(...) call that does not revert, the reference contract always leaves initialized == true after successful return, whereas the mutant can make initialized == true earlier and thus behave differently when initialize reentrantly observes initialized during its execution (specifically, if a reentrant call to initialize is attempted during initialize, the reference prevents re-initialization but the mutant's earlier set may change observable state mid-initialize); the test triggers this by reentering initialize from a helper during the first initialize call and asserting that after the top-level initialize returns the initialized getter is true (which the reference preserves for all inputs but the mutant can break for some fuzzed inputs).
